story.value: Thallium's name comes from the Greek word thallos, meaning "green shoot" or "twig", because of the bright green line in its spectrum.
Thallium was discovered in 1861 by William Crookes, an English physicist and chemist.
Thallium metal was isolated in 1862 by both Crookes and Lamy, at about the same time.

uses.value: Thallium sulfide, thallium iodide and thallium bromide are compounds used in devices that detect infrared radiation.
Thallium sulfide, whose electrical conductivity changes when exposed to infrared light, is used in photocells.
Thallium oxide has been used to make glasses with a high index of refraction.
Thallium, used together with sulfur or selenium and arsenic, forms glass that melts at a low temperature.
